reports.title: Clarks Hill Lake fishing report
reports.text:
The bass bite on the lake has been good the last few weeks. Finding humps at the mouths of creeks has been the ticket to a really good day of bass fishing. Bass are now following forage into shallower areas of the lake and into creeks. Channels in the lake that transition to flats or those humps are good places for bass to chase baitfish up from deeper water.
The cooler temperatures will encourage crappie feeding and will get them moving off their summer brush piles. Finding areas of baitfish on the lake is the key to finding the crappie right now. reports.title: Lake Sinclair fishing report
reports.text: LAKE SINCLAIR IS DOWN 1.8 FEET, 70’S – Bass fishing is fair.

reports.title: Lake Russell fishing report
reports.text: LAKE RUSSELL IS DOWN 1.7 FEET, 70’S – Bass fishing is fair. Spotted bass are roaming up on the points and flats all during the day and retreating to deep-water stump beds. Either way, these bass can be caught all day long. Try the deeper water for some of the bigger bass.

reports.title: Lake Oconee fishing report
reports.text: LAKE OCONEE IS FULL, 70’S – Bass fishing is good. The water has cooled, and the bait and bass have moved into the back of the coves and creeks. Bass fishing is good.

reports.title: Lake Jackson fishing report
reports.text: LAKE JACKSON IS FULL, 70’S – Bass fishing is fair. Spotted bass are after the spinnerbaits on windy points.

reports.title: Public Fishing Area Report fishing report
reports.text:
Largemouth: Bass are moving into shallower water as the temperatures decrease this month. Bass should respond well to spinner baits and crank baits.
Crappie: The crappie are not up shallow yet. Fishing over suspended brush is your best bet. Use jigs tipped with minnows. We have noticed crappie at depths of 10 – 20 ft, but suspended.
Shad-style lures would likely be good for both largemouth and hybrids.
McDuffie angler checks in with nice largemouth.
Largemouth on the PFA have been active and caught on spinnerbaits, glide baits, and crankbaits. Targeting structure in shallower waters and transition areas has been good for anglers to catch bass.

reports.title: Reservoir Report fishing report
reports.text: This state-managed trophy bass lake was not kind to me again this week. I landed one small bass & several Bluegills.

reports.title: Lake Allatoona fishing report
reports.text:
Anglers’ successful crappie catch
Bass (courtesy of Ken Sturdivant, Southern Fishing ):
Bass fishing is good. Fish are deep to 20 feet deep and any main lake point can be a hot spot. The trick is to fish them all and break out the good ones and work them with several baits. There are a few small fish a little shallower, but they strike baits so lightly. Try the Zoom finesse worm in natural blue or Limeade. With all the deep fish, there is little to no schooling, and we can blame almost anything but its turnover. All the deep fish start at the 25-foot range. reports.title: Lake Hartwell fishing report
reports.text:
Bass (courtesy of Guide Lane Clark, (864)-254-8614; report via SCDNR Freshwater Fishing Trends ):
Bass (courtesy of Ken Sturdivant, Southern Fishing ):
Bass fishing is fair. There is a good topwater bite in the shallows, but these are all small fish. Casting to the bank is not where the fish are until midday. Better fish are at 15 feet on average. Chug Bugs, Whoppler Ploppers, and jerkbaits at daylight, then Ned rigs and Shakey heads on points and in small cuts close by at 15 feet. This is mostly Spotted Bass, so scale down. reports.title: Lake Lanier fishing report
reports.text:
Bass (courtesy of Phil Johnson, (770) 366-8845 or pjohnson15@hotmail.com; report via Southern Fishing ):
Dashawn Johnson on Lake Lanier catching Largemouth Bass and Spotted Bass.
Bass fishing on Lake Lanier is good. The lake is currently a little over a foot below full pool, and the water temperature is running in the low seventies. Overall, the lake is clear. The fall patterns are setting up, and the bass are feeding up for the winter, but it is still somewhat up and down on catching them. Wind and bait have been the key factors over the last week. reports.text: The native plants will help with bank stabilization, reduce erosion, and provide habitat for sportfish like largemouth bass and bluegill.

reports.title: Lake Weiss fishing report
reports.text:
Bass (courtesy of Ken Sturdivant, Southern Fishing ):
Bass are starting to move shallow on secondary points and in the backs of the coves following the shad movement. Spotted Bass are being caught on the old river channel ledges in 4 to 8 feet of water.

reports.title: West Point Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Bass (courtesy of Ken Sturdivant, Southern Fishing ):
Bass fishing is good. Shad are headed for the creeks, and it’s about time for the bass to follow along in big numbers. The best bite through late week was up the river on the crankbaits. Find the fish around the shad. Once the bass get into the creeks in full force, it’ll be a good opportunity for crankbaits and spinnerbaits. Rat L Traps and Rapala Shad Raps should be good patterns. Hit the banks, throwing at any piece of wood. Make accurate casts to maximize the chances for a hookup. Buzz baits in the morning will draw some strikes also. Fish are schooling like crazy in the shallows just before sunset. There are mostly hybrids and white…

reports.title: River Report fishing report
reports.text:
With water in the mid-70s to low 70s, we’ve been getting bass on olive, white, and black Boogle Bugs or MFC poppers.
Bass & Striper Fishing: Some places have dropped to the mid-to-low 60s, and we’ve been catching better quality fish on bigger baitfish patterns.

reports.title: Wes’ Hot Fly List: fishing report
reports.text: River bass: crittermite, hairy fodder, thrasher, leggy boi, clouser, stealth bomber, or Boogle bug in the afternoon.
